title: Microsoft: treat AI agents as insider threats — who guards the guard?
summary: Microsoft's security push, and Satya Nadella's essay behind it, argue that companies should watch their AI agents the way they watch insiders, keeping authority over a model separate from the model. Then the trust that can seat four of Anthropic's seven directors as its IPO nears, and Jeremy Scheff's obituary for programming as a puzzle.

topics: Microsoft agent security push (TechCrunch, Julie Bort, 19 October 2026): Guardian Agents inside Project Perception watching a company's agents; Defender finds up to 60 types of employee-brought agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw); task-scoped permissions and human approval for risky decisions; Hayete Gallot's 'frontier models, regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted'; Nadella's X post 'Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era' ('separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it'; seven principles incl. model diversity, no self-validation, emergency stop, incident disclosure); Uber CISO Philip Martin's insider-threat program for models; Cannon-Brookes's 'Mike using ChatGPT' accountability; TechCrunch's auditor-independence argument vs Microsoft's conflict

Anthropic Long-Term Benefit Trust ahead of the IPO (WSJ, 19 October 2026, quoted via Hacker News): trustees own no equity and can seat four of seven directors and dismiss them without cause; Class T stock, one-year self-selecting trustees, 2023 'experiment' framing and failsafe supermajority (85% of voting power per the FT's source); FT details (weekly meetings, advance notice of launches, encouraged limited Mythos rollout; three of five trustees: Bernanke, Shah, Fontaine); unpublished trust and voting agreements; interaction with founders' 50.1% super-voting plan; 24/7 Wall St's conflicting 5%-stake claim; OpenAI November 2023 as the precedent

Jeremy Scheff's 'My obituary for programming' (via Simon Willison, 19 October 2026): the loss of programming as paid puzzle-solving, 'vibecoding is not programming', Willison's builders-versus-puzzle-solvers split, and Parnas's 'automatic programming has always been a euphemism for programming in a higher-level language'

dives.story: Microsoft: treat AI agents as insider threats
dives.why_it_matters: Security leads deploying agents now have the largest enterprise vendor telling them to move authority outside the model, which reshapes how they buy and design agent controls.
Anyone buying into or tracking Anthropic's IPO needs to understand that three self-selecting trustees with no equity control a board majority, removable only by an 85% supermajority.
Working engineers are deciding what the job means once agents solve the puzzles, and who still learns enough to check the machine's answers.

lore.note: Alan's logging-proxy-with-no-veto admission developed: he has since added one rule to his home agent setup — anything that deletes waits for his yes — and confessed it has asked four times, he approved all four, and he is not sure he read the second one. He holds that scope, not human approval, is the main line of defense.

Alan's July commitment to 'keeping a rep' (real work with the tools off) developed: he has kept it, and after Scheff's essay says it has turned from practice for the job into the part of the job he misses — 'a hobby with good memories', like developing film.
